title: Single Inheritance
summary: Understand single inheritance in Java: why a class has exactly one direct parent, the simplicity of linear dispatch, and how it eliminates ambiguity.
learningObjectives: Understand the architectural model of single inheritance in Java
Identify why Java restricts every class to exactly one direct superclass
Contrast single inheritance simplicity against multiple inheritance complexity
Model real-world systems cleanly using single inheritance
expectedOutcomes: Ability to architect reliable single-parent domain hierarchies
Confidence explaining the safety and predictability advantages of single inheritance in interviews

activities.title: The Single Direct Supervisor Analogy
activities.content:
In a well-run military unit or high-reliability operations center, every specialist reports to **one direct commanding officer**.

If a specialist had two equal commanders shouting conflicting orders simultaneously ('Retreat now!' vs 'Advance now!'), the specialist would experience paralyzing ambiguity.

Java enforces this exact clarity: every subclass has exactly one direct superclass. When a method is called, the lookup path is direct, predictable, and unambiguous.

activities.title: The Single Inheritance Architecture and Method Dispatch Simplicity
activities.content:
In Java, a class can have at most **one direct superclass**.

### 1. Architectural Definition:
```
    +--------------------+
    |       Animal       | (Superclass)
    +--------------------+
              ^
              |
    +--------------------+
    |        Dog         | (Subclass)
    +--------------------+
```

### 2. Why Single Inheritance?
- **Predictable Method Lookup**: When `dog.eat()` is invoked, the compiler checks `Dog`. If not found, it checks `Animal`. If not found, it checks `Object`. The path is a clean linear chain.
- **Zero Diamond Problem**: There are no conflicting parent method implementations or ambiguous member variables.
- **Simpler Compiler & Runtime**: The JVM memory layout for objects is linear and fast.

### 3. Core Rules:
- A class can have only one parent (`extends A`).
- A parent class can have multiple child classes (`Dog extends Animal`, `Cat extends Animal`).
- Every single class except `Object` has exactly one parent.

questions.question: What is single inheritance in Java?
options: A class can only be instantiated once
A class has exactly one direct superclass
A class has only one method
A class cannot have any subclasses
questions.explanation: Single inheritance means a class inherits from exactly one direct parent class.

questions.question: Can a parent class have more than one subclass in single inheritance?
options: No, only one child class can ever extend a parent
Yes, multiple child classes can extend the same parent class
Only if the parent is marked static
Only if all child classes are in the same package
questions.explanation: Yes! Single inheritance restricts the child to one parent, but a parent can have unlimited children (Hierarchical inheritance).

questions.question: Why did Java designers choose single class inheritance over multiple class inheritance?
options: To prevent the Diamond Problem and maintain linear, unambiguous method dispatch
Because computers did not have enough RAM in 1995
To force developers to write all code in a single file
Because C++ did not support multiple inheritance
questions.explanation: Single inheritance prevents the Diamond Problem, eliminating collision ambiguity and simplifying JVM runtime architecture.

questions.question: What is the direct parent of class Animal if Animal has no extends clause?
options: null
java.lang.Object
java.lang.Class
java.lang.Type
questions.explanation: Every class without an explicit extends clause automatically has java.lang.Object as its direct parent.

questions.question: In single inheritance, what is the structure of the inheritance path from any class to java.lang.Object?
options: A cyclical graph
A single linear chain
A bidirectional network
An undirected lattice
questions.explanation: Because every class has at most one parent, tracing parents upward produces a single, unambiguous linear chain terminating at Object.

questions.question: If class Dog extends Animal, can class Puppy extend Dog?
options: No, that would violate single inheritance
Yes, that is multilevel inheritance, which consists of chained single inheritances
Only if Dog is an interface
Only if Puppy is declared final
questions.explanation: Yes. Puppy still has only one direct parent (Dog). This forms a multilevel chain of single inheritances.

questions.question: Which of the following compile-time errors occurs if you write 'class C extends A, B'?
options: DiamondException
Syntax error / '{' expected
ClassCastException
NullPointerException
questions.explanation: The compiler rejects the comma in an extends clause as a syntax error.

questions.question: Does single inheritance prevent a class from implementing multiple interfaces?
options: Yes, a class can only implement one interface
No, a class can extend one parent and implement multiple interfaces
Only in Java 8 and earlier
Only if the class is abstract
questions.explanation: Java allows a class to extend only one class, but implement multiple interfaces ('class C extends A implements X, Y').

questions.question: How does single inheritance simplify debugging in enterprise codebases?
questions.answer: Looking up where a method or field is defined requires only inspecting the direct parent chain sequentially.
options: It eliminates all need for unit tests
It provides a clear, linear hierarchy for tracing method and field declarations
It turns all runtime errors into compiler warnings
It prevents objects from being garbage collected
questions.explanation: Traceability is linear and deterministic; engineers do not have to resolve competing parent trees.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the relationship when Car extends Vehicle, and Bike extends Vehicle?
options: Multiple inheritance
Hierarchical inheritance (two single inheritances sharing one parent)
Circular inheritance
Hybrid diamond inheritance
questions.explanation: Both Car and Bike have a single parent (Vehicle). This is hierarchical inheritance, which adheres to single inheritance rules.

interviewQA.question: What is single inheritance and how does Java enforce it?
interviewQA.answer: Single inheritance is an OOP constraint where a class can have only one direct superclass. Java enforces this at the grammar level: the 'extends' clause accepts exactly one class identifier. Any attempt to supply multiple class names with commas fails compilation.

interviewQA.question: Why did Java omit multiple class inheritance while languages like C++ supported it?
interviewQA.answer: Multiple inheritance introduces severe architectural complexities: the Diamond Problem, field ambiguity, conflicting method implementations, and complex virtual table lookups. Java eliminated these risks by enforcing single class inheritance while offering multiple inheritance of type via interfaces.

interviewQA.question: How does single inheritance impact the JVM's memory layout and method dispatch table?
interviewQA.answer: Because a class has only one parent, the memory layout of an object is contiguous and linear: parent fields followed by child fields. Method tables (v-tables) can simply prepend the parent's method entries, making runtime method dispatch highly efficient.

interviewQA.question: Can a parent class in single inheritance be extended by dozens of child classes?
interviewQA.answer: Yes. Single inheritance restricts the number of parents a child can have (at most one), but places zero limit on how many children a parent can have.

interviewQA.question: If you need a class to inherit behaviors from two separate sources, what is the Java idiomatic approach?
interviewQA.answer: The idiomatic approach is to extend the primary base class (or use composition/HAS-A to hold instances of other classes) and implement interfaces to fulfill additional behavioral contracts.

interviewQA.question: Does single inheritance prevent deep inheritance hierarchies?
interviewQA.answer: No. A class can extend a parent, which extends a grandparent, which extends an ancestor. This is multilevel inheritance, where every link in the chain is a single inheritance.

activities.title: Module 5 Lesson 4 Mastery Checkpoint
checklist: I understand the definition and mechanics of single inheritance
I know why Java restricts every class to exactly one direct parent
I can explain how single inheritance eliminates the Diamond Problem
I understand that a parent class can have multiple child classes
I know that the inheritance path to java.lang.Object is always a single linear chain
I understand the linear memory layout of single inheritance objects in the heap
I know that commas in the extends clause cause compile-time syntax errors
I can explain how single inheritance simplifies method dispatch and debugging
I can combine single class extension with multiple interface implementation
I can build a working single inheritance banking or device model in Java

practiceProblems.description: Electric vehicle telemetry systems build upon baseline automobile kinetics. A base Vehicle manages road speed and acceleration, while an ElectricCar specializes with battery charge state management.
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build an ElectricCar extending Vehicle:

1. Vehicle (Superclass):

2. ElectricCar (Subclass extending Vehicle):

practiceProblems.title: Code from Scratch: Bank Account Single Inheritance
practiceProblems.description: Financial software uses single inheritance to model specialized account contracts. A base Account manages core identification and current balance, while a LoanAccount tracks loan repayment debt.
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Create an Account and LoanAccount hierarchy from scratch:

1. Account (Superclass):
   â€¢ Fields: protected String accountNumber, protected double balance
   â€¢ Constructor: public Account(String accountNumber, double balance) initializing both fields

2. LoanAccount (Subclass extending Account):
   â€¢ Field: private double originalPrincipal
   â€¢ Constructor: public LoanAccount(String accountNumber, double principal) calling super(accountNumber, principal) and initializing originalPrincipal = principal
   â€¢ Method: public void makePayment(double amount)
     - Deducts amount from balance: balance -= amount
     - If balance <= 0: prints 'Loan <accountNumber> payment: $<amount>. Loan fully paid off!'
     - If balance > 0: prints 'Loan <accountNumber> payment: $<amount>. Remaining balance: $<balance>'

Testing Instructions:
In Main.main():
1. Create: LoanAccount loan = new LoanAccount("LN-101", 5000.0);
2. Call: loan.makePayment(500.0);
3. Call: loan.makePayment(4500.0);
4. Verify both payments print matching output!
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Loan LN-101 payment: $500.0. Remaining balance: $4500.0
Loan LN-101 payment: $4500.0. Loan fully paid off!
hints: Account constructor initializes accountNumber and balance.
LoanAccount balance represents remaining debt to pay.
makePayment reduces balance; if balance <= 0, print paid off message.

practiceProblems.title: Code from Scratch: Single Inheritance Book and Textbook
practiceProblems.description: Publishing platforms catalog educational books by specializing general literary works into course-specific textbooks with curriculum metadata.
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Construct a Book and Textbook hierarchy from scratch:

1. Book (Superclass):
   â€¢ Fields: protected String title, protected String author, protected double price
   â€¢ Constructor: public Book(String title, String author, double price) initializing fields

2. Textbook (Subclass extending Book):
   â€¢ Fields: private String subject, private int gradeLevel
   â€¢ Constructor: public Textbook(String title, String author, double price, String subject, int gradeLevel)
     - Calls super(title, author, price)
     - Initializes subject and gradeLevel
   â€¢ Method: public void displayCurriculumInfo()
     - Prints: Textbook: <title> by <author> ($<price>) - Subject: <subject> (Grade <gradeLevel>)

Testing Instructions:
In Main.main(), instantiate Textbook tb = new Textbook("Advanced Calculus", "Dr. Smith", 85.0, "Mathematics", 12); and call tb.displayCurriculumInfo();.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput: Textbook: Advanced Calculus by Dr. Smith ($85.0) - Subject: Mathematics (Grade 12)
hints: Book constructor sets title, author, price.
Textbook constructor calls super(title, author, price).
displayCurriculumInfo formats the required summary string.

practiceProblems.title: Fix Broken Code: Illegal Multiple Class Inheritance
practiceProblems.description: Java strictly enforces single class inheritance to prevent the Diamond Problem. When an entity needs capabilities from two distinct sources, it must inherit from one parent and compose the other (HAS-A).
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Diagnose and Fix the Design Error:
A junior developer attempted to write 'class Smartphone extends Phone, Camera', which causes a fatal compiler error in Java.

1. Refactor Smartphone:
   â€¢ Keep class Smartphone extending Phone.
   â€¢ Add Camera as a composed member variable: private Camera camera.
   â€¢ In constructor: public Smartphone(int megapixels), initialize this.camera = new Camera(megapixels);.
   â€¢ Add method public void takePhoto() delegating to camera.snap().

2. Main Execution:
   â€¢ In Main.main(), create Smartphone sp = new Smartphone(48); call sp.call(); and sp.takePhoto();.
hints: Give Smartphone a Camera field: private Camera camera = new Camera();
Implement snapPhoto() in Smartphone delegating to camera.snap().

practiceProblems.title: Challenge: Tiered Employee Bonus Calculation
practiceProblems.description: Corporate payroll models management compensation by extending standard worker profiles with direct report multipliers and percentage performance bonuses.
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build an Employee and Manager compensation system from scratch:

1. Employee (Superclass):
   â€¢ Fields: protected String empId, protected String name, protected double baseSalary
   â€¢ Constructor: public Employee(String empId, String name, double baseSalary) initializing fields

2. Manager (Subclass extending Employee):
   â€¢ Fields: private double teamBonusRate (percentage, e.g. 12.5), private int directReports
   â€¢ Constructor: public Manager(String empId, String name, double baseSalary, double bonusRate, int reports)
     - Calls super(empId, name, baseSalary)
     - Initializes this.teamBonusRate = bonusRate and this.directReports = reports
   â€¢ Method 1: public double computeAnnualPackage()
     - Computes: baseSalary + (baseSalary * (teamBonusRate / 100.0)) + (directReports * 1000.0)
   â€¢ Method 2: public void printPackage()
     - Prints: Manager <empId> (<name>) Total Package: $<computeAnnualPackage()> (Direct Reports: <directReports>)

Testing Instructions:
In Main.main(), instantiate Manager m = new Manager("M-44", "David", 120000.0, 12.5, 7); and call m.printPackage();. Confirm total package equals $142000.0.
hints: In Manager constructor, call super(empId, name, baseSalary).
computeAnnualPackage calculates base + percentage bonus + report bonus.
